newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks set record highs, tech stocks surge.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks set record highs, tech stocks surge.

text.p: A buying spree in technology sent U.S. stocks sailing into record territory on Tuesday with the Dow industrials, Standard & Poor's 500 and Nasdaq Composite scoring all-time closing highs.

The Dow erased early losses and rose 38 to finish unofficially at 7383, the second straight session it toppled records. A lynchpin of the average's strength was International Business Machines Corp, which surged 5-5/8 to an all-time high of 179.
Analysts and traders said the rally in technology stocks came after an influential analyst made positive comments on Micron Technology Inc, which jumped 4-3/8 to 42-5/8.

"All the action was in technology today -- it's contagious. When you like one, you like the group, both first and second tier. That's the momentum that got things going," said Kenneth Ducey, director of trading at BT Securities.
Merrill Lynch's Tom Kurlak, a long-time bull, said he expected Micron to earn even more in 1997 and 1998 than he previously expected.

The demand for tech stocks, especially semiconductors, send the Nasdaq surging. The index crossed the 1,400 threshold for the first time and finished up 19, or 1.4 percent, to 1409. Microsoft, Intel and Dell Computer flirted with closing in record territory.
The gains came despite a sagging Treasury market, where the yield on the 30-year issue moved above 7.0 percent, the point at which many money managers switch funds into bonds.
"That's the magic number that makes a lot of people nervous but people are still following the momentum, and it is strong, until it shows signs of slowing," Ducey said.
The 30-year U.S. Treasury bond was off 15/32 in late trading to yield 7.03 percent. Prices sagged early in the session after news that U.S. consumer confidence hit a 28-year high in May.
Still, semiconductor stocks soared, led by Micron. Intel Corp jumped 6-2/16 to close at 169-5/16 and hit an intraday high of 169-3/8. Advanced Micro Devices Inc and Applied Materials Inc also rose.
The rally lifted networking stocks, including 3Com Corp, and computer stocks. Dell rose 6 to 113-1/4 and scored a fresh high of 113-5/8 in intraday trading.
AT&T Corp rose after a report that it might merge with local telephone company SBC Communications Inc. AT&T added 1-3/8 to 37-1/2 and SBC climbed 3/4 to 57-5/8.

The strength in technology masked weakness in other interest-rate sensitive areas such as transports and utilities. Tobacco stocks also fell amid news that progress had been made in negotiations between the industry and state governments over a global settlement of litigation.
Banks could not escape weakness in bonds. Citicorp fell 4-5/8 to 113-1/4. BankAmerica Corp lost 3-1/2 to 114-1/8 and J.P Morgan & Co slid 1-3/8 to 103-3/8.

Arun Kumar, U.S. equities strategist at Lehman Brothers, said stocks and bonds took different directions Tuesday because the Treasury market is "still not comfortable with the view that low unemployment and low inflation can peacefully coexist. But stocks are comfortable with that."
Coca-Cola Enterprises slipped 1/4 to 19-5/8 after it agreed to buy two North American bottlers for $1.66 billion.
About 439 million shares were traded on the New York Stock Exchange. Decliners outnumbered advancers 1,299 to 1,222.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 37.50 to officially close at 7383.41, a record.
The S&P 500 rose 2.68 to 849.71, a record.
The Nasdaq officially closed up 19.49 to 1409.21.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1881))
